title: Company launches investigation into claims Wainwright nurse's job was threatened
summary: A federal government contractor says it is launching a "full investigation" into allegations that a Wainwright, Alta., nurse's job was threatened after she was photographed with Conservative Leader…

image.caption: This photo of nurse Maureen Carpenter was posted online by Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre on Oct. 20, 2026. (Pierre Poilievre/Facebook)

blocks.text: Politics·New

A federal government contractor says it is launching a "full investigation" into allegations that a Wainwright, Alta., nurse's job was threatened after she was photographed with Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre.
Poilievre says incident followed being photographed with Conservative leader
Calian Health said in a statement on Friday that it will take action if the allegations are verified in its investigation.

"We have initiated a full investigation into the facts and circumstances of the incident. We will take appropriate action should the investigation identify conduct that is inconsistent with our values," the statement said.
In an unusual speech in the House of Commons on Wednesday evening, Poilievre said his parliamentary privilege is being breached because of the incident.

Last month, Maureen Carpenter — a nurse who helped treat soldiers burned in the CFB Wainwright fire — was photographed speaking to Poilievre following the tragic incident that killed five soldiers and wounded 38 others on Oct. 17.
'My intention was not for this to be politicized': Poilievre raises rare point of privilege

"Maureen spoke to me on base, with the permission of the unit commander. I had the permission of the base commander to be there. She talked about caring for our men and women on the shift that night, that horrendous night," said Poilievre.
The base is part of Poilievre's federal riding of Battle River-Crowfoot.

He said, following the meeting, Carpenter was subject to a complaint and threatened — told by her boss that if her term contract was not already coming to an end, she would be put under the microscope by the company's legal department.

"We owe Maureen, as well as colleagues like her, our greatest gratitude. That is what I conveyed in our conversation. Instead, Maureen tells me that she's been threatened by Calian Health, all because she spoke to her local member of Parliament," Poilievre said.

Poilievre said being able to speak to an MP is a right guaranteed under the Charter, and a requirement in order to ensure Canadians get good government. During the conversation, he said they discussed better support for mental health following the fires.
Calian said in its Friday statement that the company "fully supports individuals' rights to engage with elected representatives."
Defence minister agrees with Poilievre on concerns about threats made against constituent
Defence Minister David McGuinty said Thursday during a House committee that he asked his deputy to raise the issue with Calian, but beyond that there is little more that he could do at this point.

McGuinty said it wouldn't be appropriate for a federal minister to get involved in a private contract. He said the fact that the incident has been raised as a matter of privilege also impacts what actions he can take.

"I can't cross a certain other line, which is the question of, now, this claim that Mr. Poilievre's own privileges have been affected. That's now residing with the Speaker and I'm hoping for a good outcome in terms of the decision there," he said.
Poilievre said on Wednesday that he didn't want the incident "to be politicized. I simply wanted it to be solved."
"Ideally though, the government and Calian will instead simply say sorry and fix the problem," he said.
